benchmarks.task_description:
Fix flaky Processing Apply test that set the polarity without the manual flag

`test_processing_button_copies_only_the_polarity_as_chosen_by_hand` failed under load with `assert True is False`. The test was wrong, not the application.

The test stored `black_on_white=False` on the current page without the manual flag. Switching to Output starts a render, and that render measures the page's polarity. The generated pages are printed black on white, so when the render ended before Apply (as it can on a loaded machine), it set the current page back to True, which is correct for an unflagged value. Apply then copied True to every target.

I reproduced it by waiting for the renders between the test's `set_params` and the Apply click. The copied polarity then came out True every time, with the reported assertion.

No application change. A polarity that the user sets, with the checkbox or with Apply, carries `black_on_white_set_manually`, and `Settings.set_detected_black_on_white` leaves those alone under its lock. Every Output params writer either holds that lock or runs on the GUI thread, as Apply does.

## Test change

The test now unticks **Black on white mode** with its checkbox, as a user does. It forces both orderings:
- it waits for every render before Apply;
- after Apply it measures each target as printed, as a late render would.

The targets keep the copied False in both cases.

## Loop counts

`tests/ui/test_window_actions.py` 20 times under `-n 4`:

| | Runs failed |
|---|---|
| Before | 0 of 20; the failure only came with other suites running alongside |
| After | 0 of 20 |

The forced ordering above fails the old test every time and passes the new one.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## 이번에 한 일
- develop 배포의 "Pull & up on EC2" 에서 이미지를 받기 전에 `docker image prune -af` 로 컨테이너가 쓰지 않는 이미지를 모두 지웁니다. 지금 도는 컨테이너의 이미지는 남습니다

- 디스크 사용량(`df -h /`, `docker system df`)을 배포 로그에 남깁니다

Closes #322

- `--filter "until=72h"` 로 최근 이미지를 남기는 방법도 있지만 하루에 배포가 수십 번이라 그것만으로도 디스크가 찰 수 있어 모두 지웠습니다

benchmarks.task_description:
Do not use column min/max stats to prove that all rows in a file match

## Problem

For UPDATE/DELETE, pg_lake checks whether every row in a data file matches the filter, and if so it skips scanning that file and removes it outright. That check builds constraints from the file's column min/max stats. Those stats only describe the non-NULL values, so a file holding `(1), (NULL)` looks like `col1 = 1` and passes a filter such as `col1 = 1` or `col1 > 0`.

```sql
-- the file has a NULL row that does not match the filter
CREATE TABLE t (col1 int) USING iceberg;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1), (NULL);

-- removes the whole file, including the NULL row
DELETE FROM t WHERE col1 = 1;
SELECT count(*) FROM t;  -- 0, expected 1
```

## Solution

Full-match pruning now only uses column stats for columns that are declared NOT NULL. Partial-match pruning (skipping files that cannot contain matches) is unchanged, since NULLs never satisfy a strict filter. Partition bounds already produce an `IS NULL` constraint for NULL partition values, so they keep being used.

## Test plan

- New `test_pruning_deletes_with_nulls` covers equality and range filters, a DELETE through a filtered view, and `IS NULL` deletes on files with mixed NULL and non-NULL values.
- `test_pruning_deletes` now uses a NOT NULL column so it still covers the skip-scan path.
- `test_data_file_pruning.py`, `test_partition_pruning.py` and `test_modify*.py` pass locally on PG 18.

+def test_pruning_deletes_with_nulls(s3, pg_conn, extension, with_default_location):
+    explain_prefix = "EXPLAIN (verbose, format json) "
+
+    run_command(
+        """
+        CREATE SCHEMA test_pruning_deletes_nulls;
+        CREATE TABLE test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl (
+            col1 INT
+        ) USING iceberg WITH (autovacuum_enabled='False');
+
+        -- min/max of the non-NULL values match, but the file also has a NULL
+        INSERT INTO test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl VALUES (1), (NULL);
+        INSERT INTO test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl VALUES (2), (3), (NULL);
+
+        CREATE VIEW test_pruning_deletes_nulls.positive AS
+        SELECT * FROM test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl WHERE col1 > 0;
+        """,
+        pg_conn,
+    )
+    pg_conn.commit()
+
+    # column stats cannot prove that all rows match, so files must be scanned
+    results = run_query(
+        f"{explain_prefix} delete from test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl where col1 = 1",
+        pg_conn,
+    )
+    assert int(fetch_data_files_used(results)) == 1
+    assert int(fetch_data_files_skipped(results)) == 0
+
+    results = run_query(
+        f"{explain_prefix} delete from test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl where col1 > 0",
+        pg_conn,
+    )
+    assert int(fetch_data_files_used(results)) == 2
+    assert int(fetch_data_files_skipped(results)) == 0
+
+    run_command("delete from test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl where col1 = 1", pg_conn)
+    run_command("delete from test_pruning_deletes_nulls.positive", pg_conn)
+    pg_conn.commit()
+
+    results = run_query(
+        "select count(*), count(col1) from test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl", pg_conn
+    )
+    assert results[0][0] == 2
+    assert results[0][1] == 0
+
+    # the remaining files are all NULL, but nullable columns never use stats
+    # for a full match, so IS NULL also has to scan the files
+    results = run_query(
+        f"{explain_prefix} delete from test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl where col1 is null",
+        pg_conn,
+    )
+    assert int(fetch_data_files_used(results)) == 2
+    assert int(fetch_data_files_skipped(results)) == 0
+
+    run_command(
+        "delete from test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl where col1 is null", pg_conn
+    )
+    pg_conn.commit()
+
+    results = run_query("select count(*) from test_pruning_deletes_nulls.tbl", pg_conn)
+    assert results[0][0] == 0
+
+    run_command("DROP SCHEMA test_pruning_deletes_nulls CASCADE", pg_conn)
+    pg_conn.commit()
+
+

benchmarks.task_description:
[Bugfix][DSv4.1] Seed the -1 sentinel in the prefill sparse index workspace



## Overview

Port #55299 to the DeepSeek-V4.1 copy of `combine_topk_swa_indices`: seed a caller-provided `out=` buffer with the `-1` sentinel before the kernel writes each row's valid prefix. Without it, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill through FlashMLA mega attention reads stale indices and produces NaN; in our deployment this surfaced as an intermittent illegal memory access.

## Claims

- Fixes NaN attention outputs in DSv4.1 FlashMLA mega-attention prefill for rows whose combined index list is shorter than the padded width: the first 127 tokens of a fresh prompt, the rows right after an SWA bounded-replay start, and compressed-layer rows that have fewer than `index_topk` candidates.
- The NaN spreads through the KV cache into later tokens and layers, including the indexer, where `top_k_per_row_prefill` turns NaN logits into out-of-range indices (#49896). In our downstream build, which also runs the decoder replay tail as one FULL CUDA graph (not in `main`), those indices reached `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` and crashed with an illegal memory access; this fix removes that crash there.
- One line, identical to the #55299 fix in `deepseek_v4`.

## Validation

GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FlashMLA mega attention, MXFP4 indexer cache, breakable CUDA graphs (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). The kernel repro was run twice: with our vLLM 0.30-based build, and with `main`'s `cache_utils.py` (e161a0798c) loaded over it, with identical results. `main`'s combine kernel additionally masks invalid top-k candidates, but like ours it never writes `[combined_len, width)`. The E2E run used the downstream build.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel repro (below), `main`'s `combine_topk_swa_indices` + `fused_norm_rope_attn_rope_cast_fwd`, `out=` pre-filled with in-range indices of NaN KV rows; NaN output rows | 96/300 (SWA-only, width 128), 768/1200 (ratio 2, width 640), 352/700 (ratio 1, width 640) | 0 / 0 / 0, no stale tail entry |
| Same kernel, tail entries set to `-1`, out of range, or pointing at finite rows | output bit-identical in all three | n/a |
| E2E, downstream prefill serving stack, DP4/EP4 on 4x GB200; per DP rank, a fresh 600-1300-token prompt plus a prefix hit (16K-60K prefix) within 40 ms at 2 pairs/s, plus long fresh prompts | illegal memory access 2 s into the workload | 900 s, 13,801 requests; 0 illegal memory access, 0 CUDA errors |

No test is added, as in #55299: CI has no GB200 runner exercising DSv4.1 FlashMLA mega attention, so the validation above was done outside CI.

In the downstream build, a GPU core dump of the crash places it in `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` (block-table load) in the replay-tail FULL graph, and per-row NaN probes show the first real-row NaN at the layer-1 input (layer 0 is pure SWA). No accuracy eval was run: rows that never hit a stale tail are unchanged (second row of the table), and the change only restores the sentinel the kernel contract already assumes.

<details>
<summary>Kernel repro</summary>

```python
import torch

import vllm.v1.attention.ops.flashmla  # noqa: F401  registers _flashmla_C
from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops import combine_topk_swa_indices
from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.fused_layout import WV_GROUP_SIZE
from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.flash_mla_mega_attn import (
    _HEAD_DIM_V, _ROPE_ARGS, _SF_ARGS, alloc_mega_attn_output,
)

H, D, W, TOPK = 64, 512, 128, 512
dev = "cuda"
g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(0)


def case(n, top_k, ratio, comp_rows):
    m = comp_rows + n + 2048  # kv rows: compressed | swa | never written
    kv = (torch.randn(m, 1, D, device=dev, generator=g) * 0.5).bfloat16()
    kv[comp_rows + n :] = float("nan")
    q = (torch.randn(n, H, D, device=dev, generator=g) * 0.5).bfloat16()
    pos = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    col = torch.arange(TOPK, device=dev)[None, :]
    topk = torch.where(col < ((pos + 1) // max(ratio, 1))[:, None], col, -1).int()
    width = (top_k + W + 127) // 128 * 128
    # A workspace slice holding stale in-range indices from an earlier call.
    idx_ws = (comp_rows + n + torch.arange(width, device=dev)).repeat(n, 1).int()
    lens_ws = torch.empty(n, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    qsl = torch.tensor([0, n], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    seq = torch.tensor([n], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    idx, lens = combine_topk_swa_indices(
        topk, qsl, seq, seq, W, ratio, top_k, m, comp_rows, out=(idx_ws, lens_ws)
    )
    out = alloc_mega_attn_output(n, H // WV_GROUP_SIZE, torch.device(dev))
    torch.ops._flashmla_C.fused_norm_rope_attn_rope_cast_fwd(
        q, kv, idx.unsqueeze(1), D**-0.5, _HEAD_DIM_V, torch.zeros(H, device=dev),
        lens, False, 0.0, pos, *_ROPE_ARGS,
        torch.randn(65536, 64, device=dev, generator=g), H // WV_GROUP_SIZE,
        *_SF_ARGS, out.data, out.scale,
    )
    nan = ((out.data.view(torch.uint8) & 0x7F) == 0x7F).flatten(1).any(1)
    print(f"ratio={ratio} width={width} nan_rows={int(nan.sum())}/{n}")


case(300, 0, 0, 0)      # SWA-only layer
case(1200, TOPK, 2, 1024)
case(700, TOPK, 1, 1024)
```

</details>

## Details

`combine_topk_swa_indices` writes `[0, combined_len)` of each row and relies on the rest being `-1`, which `topk_length` pairs with. The `out=None` branch gets that from `torch.full(-1)`; the `out=` branch does not seed it. Both NVIDIA callers pass a workspace slice (`flash_mla_mega_attn.py` prefill, `flashmla.py`), so the tail holds whatever an earlier user of the arena left there.

The FlashMLA prefill kernel processes the index list in whole `B_TOPK` tiles (the reason for the 128 alignment) and still loads the KV rows of a tile's entries past `topk_length`, masking them to p = 0. A stale in-range index that lands on a `kv_ws` row this call did not write brings in arbitrary bytes, and 0 * NaN = NaN, so the masked entry still poisons the output row. Rows with a short window are the ones with a tail: at layer 0 (width 128) a fresh prompt's positions 0-126; in compressed layers (width 640) every row with fewer than 512 top-k candidates or a window shorter than 128 (for example right after an SWA bounded-replay start).

#55299 fixed exactly this in `deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py`. The `deepseek_v41` package was added afterwards by #56228 from an older copy of that file: its `combine_topk_swa_indices` matched the pre-#55299 V4 version line for line when it was added, and has never had the line.

Cost: one memset of `rows x width` int32 per call (about 20 MiB for an 8K-token chunk at width 640). Writing the tail inside the Triton kernel would avoid it, but would duplicate the padded-width formula in the kernel and diverge from the V4 fix; this keeps the fix the same in both packages.

Not a duplicate: open PRs touching `combine_topk_swa_indices` are ROCm-only (#60091, #56638). #59131 reworks the same prefill path but still passes the workspace as `out=`, so it depends on this fix as well.

[Ascend] Promote region bounds before overlap analysis

Casting complete int32 region expressions to int64 hides dynamic `min`/`max` tail bounds from the arithmetic simplifier. For in-place persistent RoPE kernels, the resulting overlap proofs can exhaust the Z3 budget and introduce unnecessary cross-iteration GM dependencies that serialize the pipeline.

Use `Int64Promoter` to widen region minima and extents before forming half-open endpoints. This restores tail-bound simplification while preserving 64-bit endpoint arithmetic and empty-region checks. Add regression coverage for disjoint and overlapping dynamic tiles and accesses at `INT32_MAX`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary

- Promote each region minimum and extent to `int64` before forming half-open endpoints in `RegionsMayConflict`. This lets the arithmetic simplifier reduce dynamic tail bounds while preserving 64-bit endpoint arithmetic and empty-region checks.
- Add regression coverage for dynamic tiles with disjoint and overlapping regions, plus DMA accesses near `INT32_MAX`.

- The changed C++ file is covered by `docs/developer_guide/cpp_style.md`. The change does not appear to alter a documented style rule.
